title: Keritot 9
description: How a convert enters the covenant as Israel’s ancestors did, through circumcision, immersion and the sprinkling of blood; the convert’s quarter-dinar and the ger toshav on Shabbat; and the mishna’s lists of those who bring an offering for intentional sin as for unwitting sin, and of those who bring one offering for many transgressions.
topics: 🕊️ The convert’s offering: why not a meal offering, and why not a single young bird
🌊 Circumcision, immersion and the sprinkling of blood, and accepting converts when there are no offerings
🪙 The quarter-dinar for a convert’s nest, and a ger toshav working on Shabbat
⚖️ Four who bring an offering for intentional sin as for unwitting sin: the maidservant, the nazirite and two oaths
⏱️ “Unexpectedly, suddenly”: unwitting, beyond one’s control, and intentional
👥 Five maidservants in one lapse, or one maidservant in five: separate bodies
🧺 The nazirite, the jealous husband and the leper: when one offering covers many, and when poverty or wealth is fixed
👶 A woman who gave birth to several offspring: Rabbi Yehuda counts from the first, the Rabbis from the second

a1.he: יָכוֹל שֶׁאֲנִי מְרַבֶּה אֲפִילּוּ מִנְחָה? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: ״כֵּן״.

a2.he: תַּנְיָא אִידַּךְ: ״וְעָשָׂה אִשֵּׁה רֵיחַ נִיחוֹחַ לַה׳״, שׁוֹמֵעַ אֲנִי כֹּל שֶׁעוֹלֶה לָאִשִּׁים, אֲפִילּוּ מִנְחָה? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: ״כַּאֲשֶׁר תַּעֲשׂוּ כֵּן יַעֲשֶׂה״ – מָה אַתֶּם מִינֵי דָמִים, אַף הֵם מִינֵי דָמִים.

a3.he: אִי מָה אַתֶּם עוֹלָה וּשְׁלָמִים, אַף הֵם עוֹלָה וּשְׁלָמִים! תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: ״כָּכֶם כַּגֵּר יִהְיֶה״ – לָכֶם הִקַּשְׁתִּיו, וְלֹא לְדָבָר אַחֵר, לְקׇרְבְּנוֹתֵיכֶם.

a4.he: רַבִּי אוֹמֵר: ״כָּכֶם״ – כַּאֲבוֹתֵיכֶם, מָה אֲבוֹתֵיכֶם לֹא נִכְנְסוּ לַבְּרִית אֶלָּא בְּמִילָה וּטְבִילָה וְהַרְצָאַת דָּם – אַף הֵם לֹא יִכָּנְסוּ לַבְּרִית אֶלָּא בְּמִילָה וּטְבִילָה וְהַרְצָאַת דָּמִים.

a5.he: לְהָבִיא פְּרִידָה אַחַת – אִי אֶפְשָׁר, שֶׁלֹּא מָצִינוּ בְּכׇל הַתּוֹרָה כּוּלָּהּ. לֹא אָמְרוּ קֵן אֶלָּא לְהָקֵל עָלָיו.

a6.he: וְלָא? וְהָתַנְיָא: ״וְהִקְרִיבוֹ״, מָה תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר? לְפִי שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר בְּתוֹרִים: ״וְהִקְרִיב״, שׁוֹמֵעַ אֲנִי הָאוֹמֵר: ״הֲרֵי עָלַי עוֹלַת הָעוֹף״ לֹא יִפְחוֹת מִשְּׁנֵי פְרִידִין? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: ״וְהִקְרִיבוֹ״ – אֲפִילּוּ פְּרִידָה אַחַת! – חוֹבָה מִיהָא לָא אַשְׁכְּחַן.

a7.he: וְהָאִיכָּא יוֹלֶדֶת, דְּמַתְיָא בֶּן יוֹנָה אוֹ תוֹר לְחַטָּאת! – מִשּׁוּם דְּאִיכָּא כֶּבֶשׂ בַּהֲדַהּ.

a8.he: אָמַר מָר: מָה אֲבוֹתֵיכֶם לֹא נִכְנְסוּ לַבְּרִית אֶלָּא כּוּ׳. בִּשְׁלָמָא מִילָה, דִּכְתִיב: ״כִּי מוּלִים הָיוּ כׇּל הָעָם הַיּוֹצְאִים״, אִי נָמֵי מֵהָכָא: ״וְאֶעֱבוֹר עָלַיִךְ וָאֶרְאֵךְ מִתְבּוֹסֶסֶת בְּדָמָיִךְ וָאוֹמַר לָךְ בְּדָמַיִךְ חֲיִי וְגוֹ׳״.

a9.he: הַרְצָאַת דָּמִים, דִּכְתִיב: ״וַיִּשְׁלַח אֶת נַעֲרֵי בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל״. אֶלָּא טְבִילָה מְנָלַן? דִּכְתִיב: ״וַיִּקַּח מֹשֶׁה חֲצִי הַדָּם וְיִזְרוֹק עַל הָעָם״ – וְאֵין הַזָּאָה בְּלֹא טְבִילָה.

a10.he: אֶלָּא מֵעַתָּה, הָאִידָּנָא דְּלֵיכָּא קׇרְבָּן לָא נְקַבֵּל גֵּרִים! אָמַר רַב אַחָא בַּר יַעֲקֹב: ״וְכִי יָגוּר אִתְּכֶם גֵּר אֲשֶׁר בְּתוֹכְכֶם וְגוֹ׳״.

a11.he: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: גֵּר בִּזְמַן הַזֶּה – צָרִיךְ שֶׁיַּפְרִישׁ רוֹבַע לְקִינּוֹ. אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן: כְּבָר נִמְנָה (עָלָיו) [עָלֶיהָ] רַבָּן יוֹחָנָן בֶּן זַכַּאי וּבִטְּלָהּ, מִפְּנֵי הַתַּקָּלָה. אָמַר רַב אִידִי בַּר גֵּרְשׁוֹם אָמַר רַב אַדָּא בַּר אַהֲבָה: הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן.

a12.he: וְאִיכָּא דְמַתְנֵי לַהּ עַל הָדָא, דְּתָנוּ רַבָּנַן: גֵּר תּוֹשָׁב מוּתָּר לַעֲשׂוֹת מְלָאכָה בְּשַׁבָּת לְעַצְמוֹ כְּיִשְׂרָאֵל בְּחוּלּוֹ שֶׁל מוֹעֵד.

a13.he: רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אוֹמֵר: כְּיִשְׂרָאֵל בְּיוֹם טוֹב. רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר: גֵּר תּוֹשָׁב עוֹשֶׂה בַּשַּׁבָּת לְעַצְמוֹ כְּיִשְׂרָאֵל בַּחוֹל. רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר: אֶחָד גֵּר תּוֹשָׁב וְאֶחָד עֶבֶד וְאָמָה הַתּוֹשָׁבִים עוֹשִׂין מְלָאכָה בַּשַּׁבָּת לְעַצְמָן כְּיִשְׂרָאֵל בַּחוֹל.

a14.he: מַתְנִי׳ אֵלּוּ מְבִיאִין עַל הַזָּדוֹן כַּשּׁוֹגֵג: הַבָּא עַל שִׁפְחָה, וְנָזִיר שֶׁנִּטְמָא, וּשְׁבוּעַת הָעֵדוּת, וּשְׁבוּעַת הַפִּקָּדוֹן.

a15.he: חֲמִשָּׁה מְבִיאִין קׇרְבָּן אֶחָד עַל עֲבֵירוֹת הַרְבֵּה, וַחֲמִשָּׁה מְבִיאִין קׇרְבָּן עוֹלֶה וְיוֹרֵד. אֵלּוּ מְבִיאִין קׇרְבָּן אֶחָד עַל עֲבֵירוֹת הַרְבֵּה: הַבָּא עַל שִׁפְחָה בִּיאוֹת הַרְבֵּה, וְנָזִיר שֶׁנִּטְמָא טוּמְאוֹת הַרְבֵּה.

a17.he: דְּתָנוּ רַבָּנַן: ״וְכִפֶּר עָלָיו הַכֹּהֵן בְּאֵיל הָאָשָׁם עַל חַטָּאתוֹ אֲשֶׁר חָטָא״, מְלַמֵּד שֶׁמֵּבִיא קׇרְבָּן אֶחָד עַל עֲבֵירוֹת הַרְבֵּה. ״בְּאֵיל הָאָשָׁם... וְנִסְלַח לוֹ מֵחַטָּאתוֹ אֲשֶׁר חָטָא״ – לַעֲשׂוֹת שׁוֹגֵג כְּמֵזִיד.

a19.he: דִּכְתִיב: ״וְכִי יָמוּת מֵת עָלָיו בְּפֶתַע פִּתְאוֹם״, ״פֶּתַע״ – זֶה שׁוֹגֵג, וְכֵן הוּא אוֹמֵר: ״אִם בְּפֶתַע בְּלֹא אֵיבָה הֲדָפוֹ״, ״פִּתְאוֹם״ – זֶה אוֹנֶס, וְכֵן הוּא אוֹמֵר: ״וַיֹּאמֶר ה׳ פִּתְאֹם אֶל מֹשֶׁה״.

a20.he: תַּנְיָא אִידַּךְ: ״פִּתְאוֹם״ – זֶה מֵזִיד, וְכֵן הוּא אוֹמֵר: ״עָרוּם רָאָה רָעָה וְנִסְתָּר וּפְתָאִים עָבְרוּ וְנֶעֱנָשׁוּ״.

a21.he: נִכְתּוֹב קְרָא ״פִּתְאוֹם״, דְּמַשְׁמַע שׁוֹגֵג, וּמַשְׁמַע מֵזִיד, וּמַשְׁמַע אוֹנֶס. מֵזִיד וְאוֹנֶס – כְּדַאֲמַרַן, וּמַשְׁמַע נָמֵי שׁוֹגֵג, דִּכְתִיב: ״פֶּתִי יַאֲמִין לְכׇל דָּבָר״, וְלָא נִכְתּוֹב קְרָא ״פֶּתַע״!

a22.he: אִי כְּתַב קְרָא ״פִּתְאוֹם״, דְּמַשְׁמַע שׁוֹגֵג וּמַשְׁמַע מֵזִיד וּמַשְׁמַע אוֹנֶס, הֲוָה אָמֵינָא: כִּי מַיְיתֵי קׇרְבָּן – בְּשׁוֹגֵג, מִידֵּי דְּהָוֵי אַתּוֹרָה כּוּלַּהּ, אֲבָל אוֹנֶס וּמֵזִיד אֵימָא לָא,

a23.he: כְּתַב רַחֲמָנָא ״פֶּתַע״, דְּשׁוֹגֵג הוּא, לְגַלּוֹיֵי עֲלֵיהּ דְּפִתְאוֹם דְּאוֹנֶס וּמֵזִיד הוּא, דַּאֲפִילּוּ הָכִי חַיֵּיב רַחֲמָנָא.

a24.he: שְׁבוּעַת הָעֵדוּת, מְנָלַן? דְּתָנוּ רַבָּנַן: בְּכוּלָּן נֶאֱמַר ״וְנֶעְלַם״, כָּאן לֹא נֶאֱמַר ״וְנֶעְלַם״ – לְחַיֵּיב עַל הַשּׁוֹגֵג כְּמֵזִיד.

a25.he: שְׁבוּעַת הַפִּקָּדוֹן, מְנָלַן? יָלֵיף ״תֶּחְטָא״ ״תֶּחְטָא״ מִשְּׁבוּעַת הָעֵדוּת.

a26.he: חֲמִשָּׁה מְבִיאִין קׇרְבָּן אֶחָד עַל עֲבֵירוֹת הַרְבֵּה. קָתָנֵי: הַבָּא עַל הַשִּׁפְחָה בִּיאוֹת הַרְבֵּה. מְנָלַן?

a27.he: דְּתָנוּ רַבָּנַן: ״וְכִפֶּר עָלָיו הַכֹּהֵן בְּאֵיל הָאָשָׁם עַל חַטָּאתוֹ אֲשֶׁר חָטָא״, מְלַמֵּד שֶׁמֵּבִיא קׇרְבָּן אֶחָד עַל עֲבֵירוֹת הַרְבֵּה. ״בְּאֵיל הָאָשָׁם וְנִסְלַח לוֹ מֵחַטָּאתוֹ אֲשֶׁר חָטָא״ – לַעֲשׂוֹת מֵזִיד כְּשׁוֹגֵג.

a28.he: וְהָא קְרָא, כִּי כְּתִיב – בְּמֵזִיד כְּתִיב! אֶלָּא אֵימָא: לַעֲשׂוֹת שׁוֹגֵג כְּמֵזִיד.

a29.he: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רַבִּי חֲנִינָא טִירְנָאָה מֵרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: הַבָּא עַל חָמֵשׁ שְׁפָחוֹת חֲרוּפוֹת בְּהֶעְלֵם אֶחָד, מַהוּ? חַיָּיב עַל כָּל אַחַת וְאַחַת, אוֹ אֵינוֹ חַיָּיב אֶלָּא אַחַת? אֲמַר לֵיהּ: חַיָּיב עַל כָּל אַחַת וְאַחַת.

a30.he: מַאי שְׁנָא מֵחֲמִשָּׁ[ה] הֶעְלֵמוֹת בְּשִׁפְחָה אַחַת? אֲמַר לֵיהּ: (אֵין) שִׁפְחָה אַחַת [אֵין] גּוּפִין מוּחְלָקִין, חָמֵשׁ שְׁפָחוֹת גּוּפִין מוּחְלָקִין.

a31.he: וּמְנָלַן דְּגַבֵּי שִׁפְחָה גּוּפִין מוּחְלָקִין? אֲמַר לֵיהּ: לָאו אָמְרַתְּ גַּבֵּי עֲרָיוֹת ״וְאִשָּׁה״ – לְחַלֵּק עַל כׇּל אִשָּׁה וְאִשָּׁה? גַּבֵּי שִׁפְחָה נָמֵי כְּתִיב: ״אֲשֶׁר יִשְׁכַּב אֶת אִשָּׁה שִׁכְבַת זֶרַע

b1.he: וְהִיא שִׁפְחָה״ – לְחַלֵּק עַל כׇּל שִׁפְחָה וְשִׁפְחָה.

b2.he: נָזִיר שֶׁנִּטְמָא טוּמְאוֹת הַרְבֵּה. מַאן תַּנָּא?

b3.he: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה הִיא, דְּאָמַר: נְזִירוּת דְּטׇהֳרָה מִשְּׁבִיעִי הוּא דְּחָיְילָא עֲלֵיהּ. וּמַשְׁכַּחַת לַהּ כְּגוֹן שֶׁנִּטְמָא בַּשְּׁבִיעִי, וְחָזַר וְנִטְמָא בַּשְּׁבִיעִי, וְכֵיוָן דְּלֹא יָצָא שָׁעָה הָרְאוּיָה לְהַקְרִיב בָּהּ קׇרְבָּן – אֵינוֹ חַיָּיב אֶלָּא קׇרְבָּן אֶחָד.

b4.he: דְּאִי רַבִּי, כֵּיוָן דְּאָמַר רַבִּי: נְזִירוּת דְּטׇהֳרָה עַד שְׁמִינִי לָא חָיְילָא עֲלֵיהּ, אִי דְּנִטְמָא בַּשְּׁבִיעִי וְחָזַר וְנִטְמָא בַּשְּׁבִיעִי – כּוּלַּהּ טוּמְאָה אֲרִיכְתָּא הִיא,

b5.he: אִי דְּנִטְמָא בַּשְּׁמִינִי וְחָזַר וְנִטְמָא בַּשְּׁמִינִי, כֵּיוָן דְּיָצָאת שָׁעָה שֶׁרְאוּיָיה לְהַקְרִיב קׇרְבָּן – מְחַיֵּיב עַל כׇּל אַחַת וְאַחַת! אֶלָּא שְׁמַע מִינָּה רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה.

b6.he: וּמַאי דְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה? דְּתַנְיָא: ״וְקִדַּשׁ אֶת רֹאשׁוֹ בַּיּוֹם הַהוּא״ – בְּיוֹם הֲבָאַת קׇרְבְּנוֹתָיו, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי.

b7.he: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: בְּיוֹם תִּגְלַחְתּוֹ.

b8.he: מַתְנִי׳ הַמְקַנֵּא לְאִשְׁתּוֹ עַל יְדֵי אֲנָשִׁים הַרְבֵּה וּמְצוֹרָע שֶׁנִּתְנַגַּע נְגָעִים הַרְבֵּה,

b9.he: הֵבִיא צִיפֳּרִין וְנִתְנַגֵּעַ – לֹא עָלוּ לוֹ עַד שֶׁיָּבִיא חַטָּאתוֹ, רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: עַד שֶׁיָּבִיא אֲשָׁמוֹ.

b10.he: גְּמָ׳ מְנָלַן? דִּכְתִיב: ״זֹאת תּוֹרַת הַקְּנָאוֹת״ – תּוֹרָה אַחַת לְקִנּוּיִין הַרְבֵּה.

b11.he: מְצוֹרָע שֶׁנִּתְנַגֵּעַ נְגָעִים הַרְבֵּה כּוּ׳. מְנָלַן? דִּכְתִיב: ״זֹאת תּוֹרַת הַמְּצוֹרָע״ – תּוֹרָה אַחַת לִמְצוֹרָעִים הַרְבֵּה.

b12.he: הֵבִיא צִיפֳּרִין וְנִתְנַגֵּעַ – לֹא עָלוּ לוֹ עַד שֶׁיָּבִיא חַטָּאתוֹ, רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: עַד שֶׁיָּבִיא אֲשָׁמוֹ.

b13.he: וְהָאָמְרַתְּ: אֵין מֵבִיא אֶלָּא קׇרְבָּן אֶחָד! חַסּוֹרֵי מִחַסְּרָא וְהָכִי קָתָנֵי: הֵבִיא צִיפֳּרִין וְנִתְנַגֵּעַ – אֵין מֵבִיא אֶלָּא קׇרְבָּן אֶחָד. וּלְאַקְבּוֹעֵי בַּעֲנִיּוּת וּבַעֲשִׁירוּת – לָא מִיקְּבַע, עַד שֶׁיָּבִיא חַטָּאת. רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: עַד שֶׁיָּבִיא אֲשָׁמוֹ.

b14.he: תְּנַן הָתָם: מְצוֹרָע שֶׁהֵבִיא אֲשָׁמוֹ וְהֶעֱשִׁיר – הַכֹּל הוֹלֵךְ אַחַר חַטָּאת, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן. רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: הַכֹּל הוֹלֵךְ אַחַר אָשָׁם. תַּנְיָא רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן, יַעֲקֹב אוֹמֵר: הַכֹּל הוֹלֵךְ אַחַר צִיפֳּרִין.

b15.he: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב: שְׁלָשְׁתָּן מִקְרָא אֶחָד דָּרְשׁוּ – ״אֲשֶׁר לֹא תַשִּׂיג יָדוֹ בְּטׇהֳרָתוֹ״, רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן סָבַר: דָּבָר הַמְכַפְּרוֹ, רַבִּי יְהוּדָה סָבַר: דָּבָר הַמַּכְשִׁירוֹ, רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב אוֹמֵר: דָּבָר הַגּוֹרֵם לוֹ טׇהֳרָה, וּמַאי נִינְהוּ? צִיפֳּרִין.

b16.he: מַתְנִי׳ הָאִשָּׁה שֶׁיָּלְדָה וְלָדוֹת הַרְבֵּה, וְהִפִּילָה בְּתוֹךְ שְׁמוֹנִים נְקֵבָה, חָזְרָה וְהִפִּילָה בְּתוֹךְ שְׁמוֹנִים נְקֵבָה,

b18.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: מְבִיאָה עַל הָרִאשׁוֹן וְאֵינָהּ מְבִיאָה עַל הַשֵּׁנִי. מְבִיאָה עַל הַשְּׁלִישִׁי וְאֵינָהּ מְבִיאָה עַל הָרְבִיעִי.

b19.he: גְּמָ׳ מְנָלַן? דְּתָנֵי תַּנָּא קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב שֵׁשֶׁת: ״זֹאת תּוֹרַת הַיּוֹלֶדֶת לַזָּכָר וְלַנְּקֵבָה״ – מְלַמֵּד שֶׁמְּבִיאָה קׇרְבָּן אֶחָד עַל וְלָדוֹת הַרְבֵּה. יָכוֹל אַף עַל הַלֵּידָה וְעַל הַזִּיבָה? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: ״זֹאת״.

b20.he: קָתָנֵי: יָכוֹל עַל הַלֵּידָה וְעַל הַזִּיבָה אֵינָהּ מְבִיאָה אֶלָּא קׇרְבָּן אֶחָד. אֶלָּא מֵעַתָּה, אָכְלָה דָּם וְיָלְדָה, הָכִי נָמֵי דְּאֵין מְבִיאָה אֶלָּא קׇרְבָּן אֶחָד?

b21.he: אֵימָא הָכִי: יָכוֹל עַל הַלֵּידָה שֶׁלִּפְנֵי מְלֹאת וְעַל הַלֵּידָה שֶׁלְּאַחַר מְלֹאת? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: ״זֹאת״.

b22.he: הִפִּילָה בְּתוֹךְ שְׁמוֹנִים כּוּ׳. כְּשֶׁתִּמְּצֵי לוֹמַר לְדִבְרֵי רַבִּי יְהוּדָה – וָלָד רִאשׁוֹן גּוֹרֵם וּמִוָּלָד רִאשׁוֹן מוֹנָה. לְדִבְרֵי חֲכָמִים – וָלָד שֵׁנִי גּוֹרֵם וּמִוָּלָד שֵׁנִי מוֹנָה.

b23.he: כְּשֶׁתִּמְצֵי לוֹמַר? פְּשִׁיטָא, הָכִי אִיתָא! מַפֶּלֶת תְּאוֹמִים אִיצְטְרִיךְ לֵיהּ, סָלְקָא דַעְתָּךְ אָמֵינָא בְּמַפֶּלֶת תְּאוֹמִים מוֹדֶה רַבִּי יְהוּדָה לְרַבָּנַן, קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן.

messages.text: 9a

Continued from 8b: a baraita derived from “an offering made by fire, of a pleasing aroma unto the Lord” (Numbers 15:14) that a convert may bring a bird burnt offering, since it is entirely for the Lord.
Gemara
One might have thought that I include as an option even a meal offering, which would not be entirely consumed on the altar. Therefore, the verse states: “So he shall do,” to exclude a meal offering.

notes.he: פירוש מנחת נסכים שהיא כולה לאישים:
notes.en: One might have thought that I include even a meal offering: meaning the meal offering of libations, which goes entirely to the fires [of the altar].

messages.text: The verse states: “And if a stranger sojourn with you, or whoever may be among you, throughout your generations, and will offer an offering made by fire, of a pleasing aroma unto the Lord, as you do, so he shall do” (Numbers 15:14). From this verse I would derive that he fulfills his obligation with any offering that is brought on the fire of the altar, even a meal offering.

verse.he: וְכִי־יָגוּר אִתְּכֶם גֵּר אוֹ אֲשֶׁר־בְּתוֹכְכֶם לְדֹרֹתֵיכֶם וְעָשָׂה אִשֵּׁה רֵיחַ־נִיחֹחַ לַיהֹוָה כַּאֲשֶׁר תַּעֲשׂוּ כֵּן יַעֲשֶׂה׃
verse.en: And when, throughout the ages, a stranger who has taken up residence with you, or one who lives among you, would present an offering by fire of pleasing odor to GOD—as you do, so shall it be done by

messages.text: Therefore, to negate that interpretation, the verse states: “As you do, so he shall do,” which teaches that just as you entered the covenant with types of offerings whose blood is sprinkled on the altar, so too must they, converts, bring types of offerings whose blood is sprinkled on the altar.

If so, why not derive similarly: Just as you entered the covenant with a burnt offering and a peace offering, so too, they must enter the covenant with a burnt offering and a peace offering? How is it derived that a convert may fulfill his obligation with a single burnt offering from an animal?

The verse states: “As you are, so shall the stranger be before the Lord” (Numbers 15:15). This serves to emphasize: I compared him to you in order to derive that just like you, he too must bring types of offerings whose blood is sprinkled on the altar, but I did not extend this comparison to another matter, i.e., to insist that his offerings must be identical to all of your offerings.

verse.he: הַקָּהָל חֻקָּה אַחַת לָכֶם וְלַגֵּר הַגָּר חֻקַּת עוֹלָם לְדֹרֹתֵיכֶם כָּכֶם כַּגֵּר יִהְיֶה לִפְנֵי יְהֹוָה׃
verse.en: the rest of the congregation. uncertain. There shall be one law for you and for the resident stranger; it shall be a law for all time throughout the ages. You and the stranger shall be alike before GOD;

notes.he: במקצת ולא כל קרבנותיכם ומיהו עולה מסתבר דמכשרא דכולה כליל:
notes.en: I compared him to you: in part, but not to all your offerings. However, [that he may bring] a burnt offering is reasonable, since it is fit [for him], as it is entirely burnt.

notes.he: מצי למימר כדלעיל השתא לעוף איתרבאי:
notes.en: The verse states: “As you are, so shall the stranger be”: it could have said, as above [8b]: Now that a bird was included, [would an animal not all the more so be included]?

messages.text: The offering of a convert is derived from the verse: “As you are, so shall the stranger be” (Numbers 15:15), which means as your ancestors were: Just as your ancestors entered the covenant only through circumcision and immersion in a ritual bath and the sprinkling of blood on the altar, so too they may enter the covenant only through circumcision and immersion and the sprinkling of some blood, which requires at least a bird offering.

notes.he: מפרש לקמן:
notes.en: Circumcision, immersion and the sprinkling of blood: it explains below.

notes.he: רבי אומר ככם כאבותיכם מה אבותיכם לא נכנסו לברית אלא במילה וטבילה והרצאת דמים רבי לית ליה דר' אליעזר בן יעקב דלמיכל בקדשים מייתי קרבן אלא קסבר לא מייתי אלא לאכשורי נפשיה בקהל שלא מצינו בכל התורה כולה אלא ב' פרידין:
notes.en: (Up to here belongs to 8b.) Rabbi says: “As you,” as your ancestors: just as your ancestors entered the covenant only through circumcision, immersion and the sprinkling of blood. Rabbi does not hold like Rabbi Eliezer ben Ya’akov, that he brings an offering in order to eat sacrificial food; rather, he holds that he brings it only to make himself fit to enter the congregation. For we have not found in the entire Torah [an offering of birds] other than two young birds.

messages.text: And it is impossible to bring only one young bird as an offering, as we have not found an offering of a single bird anywhere in the entire Torah. Consequently, if the requirement for the sprinkling of blood is fulfilled with a bird offering, the convert must bring at least two birds.
By contrast, if he chooses he may bring a single animal as a burnt offering, because a bird nest was stated in the Torah only in order to be lenient for him.
And is it true that we have not found an offering of an individual bird anywhere in the Torah? But isn’t it taught in a baraita:
messages.quote: we have not found an offering of a single bird anywhere in the entire Torah

messages.text: The verse states with regard to a bird sacrificed as a burnt offering: “And the priest shall sacrifice it” (Leviticus 1:15). Why must the verse state this? Since it is stated about doves: “And he shall sacrifice his offering of doves” (Leviticus 1:14), in the plural, I might derive from here that the one who says: It is incumbent upon me to bring a bird as a burnt offering, shall not bring less than two young birds.

verse.he: וְהִקְרִיבוֹ הַכֹּהֵן אֶל־הַמִּזְבֵּחַ וּמָלַק אֶת־רֹאשׁוֹ וְהִקְטִיר הַמִּזְבֵּחָה וְנִמְצָה דָמוֹ עַל קִיר הַמִּזְבֵּחַ׃
verse.en: The priest shall bring it to the altar, pinch off its head, and turn it into smoke on the altar; and its blood shall be drained out against the side of the altar.

notes.he: גבי עולת העוף דנדבה בויקרא:
notes.en: “And [the priest] shall sacrifice it”: stated about the voluntary bird burnt offering in [the book of] Leviticus.

notes.he: משמע קרבן שלם:
notes.en: “And he shall sacrifice” [vehikriv]: implies a complete offering.

notes.he: והקריבו הכהן אל המזבח שנאמר בנדבת העוף מה ת"ל והלא כבר נאמר והקריב מן התורים:
notes.en: “And the priest shall sacrifice it to the altar,” stated about the voluntary bird offering: why does the verse state it? Was it not already stated: “And he shall sacrifice of the doves”?

notes.he: שלא יפחות משנים דמיעוט תורים שנים:
notes.en: I would understand: that he should not bring fewer than two, since the least that “doves” can mean is two.

messages.text: Therefore, the verse states: “And the priest shall sacrifice it” (Leviticus 1:15), in the singular, to teach that one may bring a gift offering of even one single young bird.
In any event, we have not found an obligatory offering of just one bird.

notes.he: דאתיא פרידה אחת והני דגר חובה נינהו:
notes.en: At any rate, an obligatory [offering] we have not found: in which a single young bird is brought; and these of a convert are obligatory.

messages.text: But isn’t there the offering of a woman after childbirth, who brings a single pigeon or dove as a sin offering (Leviticus 12:6)?

verse.he: וּבִמְלֹאת ׀ יְמֵי טׇהֳרָהּ לְבֵן אוֹ לְבַת תָּבִיא כֶּבֶשׂ בֶּן־שְׁנָתוֹ לְעֹלָה וּבֶן־יוֹנָה אוֹ־תֹר לְחַטָּאת אֶל־פֶּתַח אֹהֶל־מוֹעֵד אֶל־הַכֹּהֵן׃
verse.en: On the completion of her period of purification, for either son or daughter, she shall bring to the priest, at the entrance of the Tent of Meeting, a lamb in its first year for a burnt offering, and a pigeon or a turtledove for a purgation offering.

messages.text: This is not difficult, because in that case there is a lamb with it as part of her offerings; the bird is not brought as a complete offering by itself.
The Master said: Just as your ancestors entered the covenant only through circumcision, immersion in a ritual bath, and the sprinkling of blood, converts must do the same.
messages.quote: Just as your ancestors entered the covenant only through circumcision

messages.text: Granted, they underwent circumcision prior to entering the covenant, as it is written: “For all the nation that left Egypt was circumcised” (Joshua 5:5).

verse.he: כִּי־מֻלִים הָיוּ כׇּל־הָעָם הַיֹּצְאִים וְכׇל־הָעָם הַיִּלֹּדִים בַּמִּדְבָּר בַּדֶּרֶךְ בְּצֵאתָם מִמִּצְרַיִם לֹא־מָלוּ׃
verse.en: Now, whereas all such people who came out of Egypt had been circumcised, none of those born after the exodus, during the desert wanderings, had been circumcised.

notes.he: בשעת יציאתן מלו:
notes.en: All the people who left: at the time of their departure they were circumcised.

notes.dh: דכתיב כי מולים היו כל העם
notes.he: פירוש שמלו עצמם ביציאתם ממצרים ואע"פ שאותן שהיו נימולים בימי אברהם לא מלו אותם ביציאת מצרים מ"מ מעיקרא כשמלו עצמן מלו ליכנס בברית המקום וליבדל משאר אומות וגם כי עתה טבלו:
notes.en: As it is written: “For all the people were circumcised”: meaning that they circumcised themselves at their exodus from Egypt. And although those who had been circumcised [following the practice] from the days of Abraham were not circumcised at the exodus from Egypt, nevertheless, originally, when they circumcised themselves, they circumcised in order to enter the covenant of the Omnipresent and to be separated from the other nations; and also now they immersed.

messages.text: Alternatively, it may be derived from here, a verse describing the redemption from Egypt: “And when I passed by you, and saw you wallowing in your blood, I said unto you: In your blood, live; and I said unto you: In your blood, live” (Ezekiel 16:6). The Sages interpret the double mention of blood in this verse as referring to the blood of the Paschal offering and the blood of circumcision.

verse.he: וָאֶעֱבֹר עָלַיִךְ וָאֶרְאֵךְ מִתְבּוֹסֶסֶת בְּדָמָיִךְ וָאֹמַר לָךְ בְּדָמַיִךְ חֲיִי וָאֹמַר לָךְ בְּדָמַיִךְ חֲיִי׃
verse.en: When I passed by you and saw you wallowing in your blood, I said to you: “Live despite your blood.” Yea, I said to you: “Live despite your blood.”

notes.he: דם פסח ודם מילה:
notes.en: In your blood: the blood of the Paschal offering and the blood of circumcision.

notes.he: בדם פסח ודם מילה:
notes.en: In your blood: in the blood of the Paschal offering and the blood of circumcision.

messages.text: And granted as well, they entered the covenant through the sprinkling of blood, as it is written: “And he sent the young men of the children of Israel, and they sacrificed burnt offerings, and they sacrificed peace offerings” (Exodus 24:5).

verse.he: וַיִּשְׁלַח אֶת־נַעֲרֵי בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל וַיַּעֲלוּ עֹלֹת וַיִּזְבְּחוּ זְבָחִים שְׁלָמִים לַיהֹוָה פָּרִים׃
verse.en: He designated some assistants among the Israelites, and they offered burnt offerings and sacrificed bulls as offerings of well-being to GOD.

notes.he: זריקת דמים על המזבח:
notes.en: The sprinkling [hartza’at] of blood: the sprinkling of blood on the altar.

notes.dh: וישלח את נערי בני ישראל ויעלו עולות
notes.he: ואע"ג דפליגי התם בפרק פרת חטאת (זבחים קטו) איכא דאמרי עולת ראייה הואי ואיכא דאמרי עולת תמיד [הואי] י"ל שהקריבו הרבה עולות:
notes.en: “And he sent the young men of the children of Israel, and they offered burnt offerings”: and although they disagree there, in the chapter Parat Ḥatat (Zevaḥim 115b), some saying it was the burnt offering of appearance and some saying it was the daily burnt offering, one can say that they offered many burnt offerings.

messages.text: But from where do we derive that immersion in a ritual bath was also part of the process of entering the covenant?
As it is written: “And Moses took half the blood…and sprinkled it on the people” (Exodus 24:6–8), and there is no sprinkling of sacrificial blood without immersion.

verse.he: וַיִּקַּח מֹשֶׁה חֲצִי הַדָּם וַיָּשֶׂם בָּאַגָּנֹת וַחֲצִי הַדָּם זָרַק עַל־הַמִּזְבֵּחַ׃ וַיִּקַּח סֵפֶר הַבְּרִית וַיִּקְרָא בְּאׇזְנֵי הָעָם וַיֹּאמְרוּ כֹּל אֲשֶׁר־דִּבֶּר יְהֹוָה נַעֲשֶׂה וְנִשְׁמָע׃ וַיִּקַּח מֹשֶׁה אֶת־הַדָּם וַיִּזְרֹק עַל־הָעָם וַיֹּאמֶר הִנֵּה דַם־הַבְּרִית אֲשֶׁר כָּרַת יְהֹוָה עִמָּכֶם עַל כׇּל־הַדְּבָרִים הָאֵלֶּה׃
verse.en: Moses took one part of the blood and put it in basins, and the other part of the blood he dashed against the altar. Then he took the record of the covenant and read it aloud to the people. And they said, “All that GOD has spoken we will faithfully do!” Moses took the blood and dashed it on the people and said, “This is the blood of the covenant that GOD now makes with you concerning all these commands.”

notes.he: שחטו עולות הרבה ושלמים הרבה שהספיק דמם לזרוק על כל אחד מישראל:
notes.en: “And sprinkled it on the people”: they slaughtered many burnt offerings and many peace offerings, whose blood sufficed to be sprinkled on each and every one of Israel.

notes.he: להביא גר שבא בזמן הזה להתגייר צריך טבילה:
notes.en: And there is no sprinkling without immersion: [this comes] to include a convert who comes to convert in the present time: he requires immersion.

notes.he: דכתיב ויקח משה את הדם ויזרוק על העם היינו הזאה וגמירי דאין הזאה בלא טבילה (דגמירי) דהכי כתיב והזה הטהור על הטמא ביום השלישי וביום השביעי וחטאו ביום השביעי וכבס בגדיו:
notes.en: From where do we derive immersion? For it is written: “And Moses took the blood and sprinkled it on the people”; that is sprinkling, and there is a tradition that there is no sprinkling without immersion, for so it is written: “And the pure person shall sprinkle upon the impure on the third day and on the seventh day; and on the seventh day he shall purify him, and he shall wash his clothes” (Numbers 19:19).

messages.text: If that is so, that these three rituals are required by Torah law for a convert to enter the congregation, then now, in our time, when there are no offerings, we not should have the ability to accept converts.

The verse states: “And if a stranger sojourn with you, or whosoever may be among you, throughout your generations” (Numbers 15:14). This teaches that converts may be accepted throughout the generations, even when there is no Temple and sacrificial offerings are therefore impossible.
messages.quote: when there are no offerings

verse.he: וְכִי־יָגוּר אִתְּכֶם גֵּר אוֹ אֲשֶׁר־בְּתוֹכְכֶם לְדֹרֹתֵיכֶם וְעָשָׂה אִשֵּׁה רֵיחַ־נִיחֹחַ לַיהֹוָה כַּאֲשֶׁר תַּעֲשׂוּ כֵּן יַעֲשֶׂה׃
verse.en: And when, throughout the ages, a stranger who has taken up residence with you, or one who lives among you, would present an offering by fire of pleasing odor to GOD—as you do, so shall it be done by

notes.dh: וכי יגור אתכם גר וגו' לדורותיכם
notes.he: אע"ג דליכא מקדש:
notes.en: “And if a stranger sojourn with you” … “throughout your generations”: even though there is no Temple.

notes.he: לדורותיכם כתיב דאפילו לדורותיכם בזמן שאין קרבן תקבלו גרים:
notes.en: “Throughout your generations” is written: that even throughout your generations, at a time when there is no offering, you shall accept converts.

messages.text: A convert in the present time is required to set aside a quarter of a dinar for his bird nest, so that when the Temple is rebuilt he can purchase the offering with this money.
messages.lead: § With regard to the offerings of a convert, the Sages taught in a baraita:

notes.he: דלכשיבנה בית המקדש יביא קן דאמרי' לעיל דצריך קרבן וקרבן בפחות מרובע לא אפשר להפריש דאין מצוי קן בפחות מרובע כדאמרינן במתני' ועמדו קינין ברבעתים אבל פחות לא אפשר:
notes.en: He must set aside a quarter dinar for his nest: so that when the Temple is built he will bring a nest, since we said above that he requires an offering. And it is impossible to set aside [money for] an offering with less than a quarter, for a nest is not available for less than a quarter, as we say in the mishna [above, 8a]: “And nests stood at a quarter-dinar each”; but less is not possible.

notes.he: לא דמי לזבה ויולדת דלא מפרשי משום דקרבן שלהם להכשירן בקדשים אבל גר מביא קרבן להתירו בקהל:
notes.en: He must set aside a quarter, etc.: this is not like a zava and a woman after childbirth, who do not set aside [money], because their offering serves to make them fit for sacrificial food; but a convert brings an offering to permit him to enter the congregation.

notes.he: דינר לצורך קינו שאם יבנה בהמ"ק יביא לאלתר:
notes.en: He must set aside a quarter: of a dinar for his nest, so that if the Temple is built he will bring it immediately.

messages.text: Rabban Yoḥanan ben Zakkai already assembled a panel of Sages who voted and nullified this ordinance, due to a potential mishap. If one would inadvertently use such money, he would be liable for the misuse of consecrated property.

notes.he: שלא יהנה ממנו:
notes.en: Due to a mishap: lest he derive benefit from it.

notes.he: גזרה שמא יהנה מאותן מעות והיה בא לידי מעילה:
notes.en: And nullified it due to a mishap: a decree, lest he derive benefit from that money and come to [the transgression of] misuse of consecrated property.

messages.text: The halakha is in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Shimon, who says that a convert should not set aside money for the purchase of offerings.

notes.he: דאמר גר ועבד ואמה התושבים עושין מלאכה לעצמן כישראל בחול ודוקא לעצמן ולא לאחרים:
notes.en: The halakha is in accordance with Rabbi Shimon: who says that a ger and a resident slave and maidservant perform labor for themselves as a Jew does on a weekday; and specifically for themselves, and not for others.

messages.text: And there are those who teach this statement of Rav Adda bar Ahava with regard to this case, as the Sages taught in a baraita:
messages.quote: The halakha is in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Shimon

messages.text: A gentile who resides in Eretz Yisrael and observes the seven Noahide mitzvot [ger toshav] is permitted to perform labor on Shabbat for himself in the same manner that a Jew is permitted to perform labor on the intermediate days of a Festival, i.e., only for matters that, if unattended, will result in significant loss.

notes.he: שקבל עליו שלא לעבוד עבודת כוכבים כגון נעמן:
notes.en: Ger toshav: one who accepted upon himself not to worship idols, such as Naaman.

notes.he: בדבר האבד כישראל בחולו של מועד:
notes.en: Performs labor on Shabbat for himself: in a matter that would otherwise be lost, like a Jew on the intermediate days of a Festival.

notes.dh: (לעיל. גבי) גר תושב עושה מלאכה לעצמו
notes.he: מכאן קשה לפ"ה דפרק החולץ (יבמות מח:) דקאמר וינפש בן אמתך והגר זה גר תושב פי' בקונט' שקיבל עליו שלא לעבוד עבודת כוכבים ומחלל שבת כעובד כוכבים והכא קאמר גר תושב עושה מלאכה לכן י"ל דההיא מיירי לענין שלא לעשות מלאכה עבור רבו אבל לעצמו שרי (פסק) מכאן פסק ר"י שמותר להניח לעובד כוכבים לעשות מלאכתו בשבת בבית ישראל עבור עצמו:
notes.en: [This refers to the line above:] A ger toshav performs labor for himself: from here there is a difficulty for Rashi’s explanation in the chapter HaḤoletz (Yevamot 48b), where it says: “And the son of your maidservant and the stranger may be refreshed” (Exodus 23:12), this is a ger toshav; and Rashi explained in his commentary: one who accepted upon himself not to worship idols, and who desecrates Shabbat like a gentile. And here it says that a ger toshav performs labor. Therefore one can say that that [verse] speaks of not performing labor on behalf of his master, but for himself it is permitted. (Ruling:) From here the Ri ruled that it is permitted to let a gentile perform his own labor on Shabbat in a Jew’s house, for himself.

notes.he: שקבל עליו שלא לעבוד עבודת כוכבים ולא קבל עליו שאר מצות:
notes.en: Ger toshav: one who accepted upon himself not to worship idols, and did not accept upon himself the other mitzvot.

notes.he: כלומר כיון שיש בו קצת גירות אינו עושה כל מלאכה בשבת אא"כ אין לו מה יאכל או דבר האבד:
notes.en: Like a Jew on the intermediate days of a Festival: that is, since he has some measure of conversion, he does not perform every labor on Shabbat, unless he has nothing to eat, or it is a matter that would otherwise be lost.

messages.text: A ger toshav may perform labor on Shabbat in the same manner that a Jew is permitted to perform labor on a Festival, i.e., only for the purpose of preparing food.

notes.he: אוכל נפש:
notes.en: Like a Jew on a Festival: [labor for] food.

notes.he: דנפישה בעלמא כתיב ביה ולא שביתה:
notes.en: Like a Jew on a Festival: for about him [the ger] only “refreshment” in general [yinafesh, Exodus 23:12] is written, and not “cessation” [shevita].

notes.he: דאינו עושה מלאכה אחרת אלא מכשירי אוכל נפש בלבד:
notes.en: Like a Jew on a Festival: that he performs no other labor except the preparation of food alone.

messages.text: A ger toshav may perform labor on Shabbat for himself in the same manner that a Jew is permitted to perform labor on a weekday.
Both a ger toshav and a resident male or female slave may perform labor on Shabbat for themselves in the same manner that a Jew may perform labor on a weekday.
According to this tradition, it is in relation to this baraita that Rav Adda bar Ahava said that the halakha is in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Shimon.

messages.caption: A ger toshav working on Shabbat for himself: four opinions in the baraita.

messages.text: Mishna

These individuals bring an offering for an intentional transgression in the same manner as they do for an unwitting transgression: One who engages in intercourse with an espoused maidservant, who is liable to bring a guilt offering (see Leviticus 19:20–22);
and a nazirite who became ritually impure, who is required to bring a sheep as a guilt offering and two doves or two pigeons, one as a sin offering and one as a burnt offering (see Numbers 6:9–12);

and one who falsely takes the oath of testimony, asserting that he does not have any testimony to provide on a given issue (see Leviticus 5:1); and one who falsely takes the oath on a deposit, asserting that an item belonging to another is not in his possession (see Leviticus 5:21–26).

notes.he: קרבן עולה ויורד:
notes.en: Mishna. The oath of testimony: [he brings] a sliding-scale offering.

notes.he: אשם:
notes.en: The oath on a deposit: [he brings] a guilt offering.

messages.text: There are five individuals who bring one offering for several transgressions, i.e., for violating the same transgression several times; and there are five individuals who bring a sliding-scale offering, which is determined based on the financial status of the sinner.
These are the five individuals who bring one offering for several transgressions: First, one who engages in several acts of intercourse with an espoused maidservant,
and second, a nazirite who became ritually impure due to several instances of contact with ritual impurity.
Gemara

The mishna teaches that one who engages in intercourse with an espoused maidservant brings an offering for an intentional transgression as he does for an unwitting transgression. From where do we derive this?
messages.quote: One who engages in intercourse with an espoused maidservant

messages.text: The verse states: “And the priest shall make atonement for him with the ram of the guilt offering before the Lord for his sin that he has sinned” (Leviticus 19:22). The superfluous phrase: That he has sinned, teaches that he brings one offering for several transgressions.

verse.he: וְכִפֶּר עָלָיו הַכֹּהֵן בְּאֵיל הָאָשָׁם לִפְנֵי יְהֹוָה עַל־חַטָּאתוֹ אֲשֶׁר חָטָא וְנִסְלַח לוֹ מֵחַטָּאתוֹ אֲשֶׁר חָטָא׃ {פ}
verse.en: With the ram of reparation offering the priest shall make expiation for him before GOD for the sin that he committed; and the sin that he committed will be forgiven him.

notes.he: גמ' מדמצי למיכתב על חטאתו ולישתוק וכתיב על חטאתו אשר חטא לאתויי חטאים הרבה:
notes.en: Gemara. Since it could have written “for his sin” and stopped, and it writes “for his sin that he has sinned,” [this comes] to include many sins.

notes.he: לפני ה' על חטאתו אשר חטא. מלמד מדכתיב ב' פעמים חטאתו חטאתו וכתיב ונסלח לו מחטאתו אשר חטא תרי זימני לעשות שוגג כמזיד לקרבן:
notes.en: “With the ram of the guilt offering before the Lord for his sin that he has sinned”: it teaches; since “his sin” is written twice, and “and he shall be forgiven for his sin that he has sinned” is written, twice, [it comes] to make unwitting like intentional with regard to an offering.

messages.text: Furthermore, the verse concludes: “With the ram of the guilt offering before the Lord for his sin that he has sinned; and he shall be forgiven for his sin that he has sinned.” The second occurrence of the phrase “that he has sinned” serves to render the halakha with regard to an unwitting transgression the same as it is with regard to an intentional transgression, that one brings a guilt offering in either case.

notes.he: להכי הדר כתיב תו ב' זימני חטא בר מב' זימני קמאי לעשות מזיד כשוגג:
notes.en: “And he shall be forgiven for his sin that he has sinned”: this is why it writes “sin” twice more, besides the first two times: to make intentional like unwitting. [Rashi’s wording here is “to make intentional like unwitting”; the daf at this line reads “to make unwitting like intentional.”]

messages.text: § The mishna teaches: A nazirite who became ritually impure brings an offering for an intentional transgression as he does for an unwitting transgression. From where do we derive this?
messages.quote: and a nazirite who became ritually impure

messages.text: It is as it is written with regard to a nazirite: “And if any man die unexpectedly [befeta], suddenly [pitom] beside him” (Numbers 6:9).

verse.he: וְכִי־יָמוּת מֵת עָלָיו בְּפֶתַע פִּתְאֹם וְטִמֵּא רֹאשׁ נִזְרוֹ וְגִלַּח רֹאשׁוֹ בְּיוֹם טׇהֳרָתוֹ בַּיּוֹם הַשְּׁבִיעִי יְגַלְּחֶנּוּ׃
verse.en: If someone dies suddenly nearby, defiling [a nazirite’s] consecrated hair, they shall shave their head at the time of becoming pure, shaving it on the seventh day.

messages.text: When the verse states: “Unexpectedly,” this is referring to an unwitting transgression, and similarly, it states: “But if he thrust him unexpectedly without enmity” (Numbers 35:22).

verse.he: וְאִם־בְּפֶתַע בְּלֹא־אֵיבָה הֲדָפוֹ אוֹ־הִשְׁלִיךְ עָלָיו כׇּל־כְּלִי בְּלֹא צְדִיָּה׃
verse.en: But if the person pushed them without malice aforethought or hurled any object at them unintentionally,

messages.text: And when the verse states: “Suddenly,” this is referring to circumstances beyond his control, and similarly, it states: “And the Lord spoke suddenly to Moses, and to Aaron, and to Miriam: Come out you three to the Tent of Meeting. And they three came out” (Numbers 12:4). The Lord’s speech came to them suddenly, in a manner that was beyond their control.

verse.he: וַיֹּאמֶר יְהֹוָה פִּתְאֹם אֶל־מֹשֶׁה וְאֶל־אַהֲרֹן וְאֶל־מִרְיָם צְאוּ שְׁלׇשְׁתְּכֶם אֶל־אֹהֶל מוֹעֵד וַיֵּצְאוּ שְׁלׇשְׁתָּם׃
verse.en: Suddenly GOD called to Moses, Aaron, and Miriam, “Come out, you three, to the Tent of Meeting.” So the three of them went out.

notes.he: בע"כ יצאו שלשתן ע"פ הדיבור:
notes.en: “And the Lord spoke suddenly”: the three of them went out by the divine word against their will.

notes.he: שבעל כרחם היה הדיבור עמהם:
notes.en: For it is written: “And the Lord spoke suddenly”: the divine speech was with them against their will.

messages.text: “Suddenly”; this is referring to an intentional transgression, and similarly the verse states: “A prudent man sees the evil, and hides himself; but the thoughtless pass on, and are punished” (Proverbs 22:3). The tanna interprets the expression “the thoughtless [peta’im]” as related to the word “suddenly [pitom],” and one can be punished, as the thoughtless are punished in the verse, but only for an intentional transgression.

verse.he: עָרוּם ׀ רָאָה רָעָה (ויסתר) [וְנִסְתָּר] וּפְתָיִים עָבְרוּ וְנֶעֱנָשׁוּ׃
verse.en:
One who was shrewd saw trouble and took cover;
The simple kept going and paid the penalty.

notes.he: היינו מזיד דאין עונש אלא על המזיד:
notes.en: “But the thoughtless pass on, and are punished”: this is intentional, for there is no punishment except for intentional sin.

notes.he: האי (פתאום) [פתיים] עביד ליה כמו פתאום מדכתיב ונענשו אלמא דמזיד הוה:
notes.en: “And the thoughtless [peta’im] pass on, and are punished” [the printed text has “suddenly” here and is corrected to “the thoughtless”]: he treats this “thoughtless” like “suddenly”; since it is written “and are punished,” evidently it was intentional.

messages.text: Let the verse write simply: “Suddenly [pitom],” as this term indicates unwitting transgression, and it also indicates intentional transgression, and it also indicates transgression due to circumstances beyond his control.

“Suddenly” indicates intentional transgression and transgression due to circumstances beyond his control, as the tanna said in the baraitot earlier; and it also indicates unwitting transgression, as it is written: “The thoughtless one [peti] believes every word” (Proverbs 14:15), and because he is misinformed, his transgression is unwitting. And if so, let the verse not write: Unexpected [peta].

verse.he: פֶּתִי יַאֲמִין לְכׇל־דָּבָר וְעָרוּם יָבִין לַאֲשֻׁרוֹ׃
verse.en:
The simple believe anything;
The clever ponders their course.

notes.he: ואינו מבין העיקר אלמא דשוגג הוא ואפי' הכי חייב רחמנא פתאום כמו פתי ולהכי כתבי תרוייהו:
notes.en: It is written: “The thoughtless one [peti] believes every word”: and does not understand the essential point; evidently he is unwitting. And even so the Merciful One rendered him liable; “suddenly” is like “thoughtless,” and that is why both are written.

messages.text: If the verse had written only “suddenly,” which indicates unwitting transgression, and also indicates intentional transgression, and also indicates transgression due to circumstances beyond his control, I would say: When a nazirite brings an offering, it is in a situation where he transgressed unwittingly, as is the case for all mitzvot in the entire Torah, that one is generally liable to bring an offering for an unwitting transgression; but for a transgression due to circumstances beyond his control or an intentional transgression, I would say the nazirite is not liable to bring an offering.

notes.he: אע"ג דפתאום דעלמא משמע אונס ושוגג ומזיד פתאום דנזיר ודאי מדמייתי קרבן עלה ש"מ דשוגג הוא מידי דהוה אכל התורה דרוב קרבנות על השגגה הן באין להכי כתיב פתע דהוי שוגג לגלות עליה דפתאום:
notes.en: I would have said: although “suddenly” elsewhere implies circumstances beyond one’s control, unwitting and intentional, the “suddenly” of the nazirite is certainly unwitting, since he brings an offering for it, just as in the entire Torah, where most offerings come for unwitting sins. That is why “unexpectedly,” which is unwitting, is written: to reveal about “suddenly” [that it means beyond his control and intentional].

notes.dh: ה"א כי מייתי קרבן בשוגג כו'
notes.he: תימה א"כ לכתוב קרא בשוגג:
notes.en: I would have said: when he brings an offering, it is for unwitting sin, etc.: this is puzzling: if so, let the verse write [a term meaning] unwitting.

messages.text: Therefore, the Merciful One wrote: Unexpected, which is a term that indicates unwitting transgression, in order to reveal about the word “suddenly” that it is a term that indicates transgression due to circumstances beyond his control or intentional transgression. Consequently, it teaches that even in this case the Merciful One rendered him liable to bring an offering.

§ The mishna teaches that one who falsely takes the oath of testimony brings an offering for an intentional transgression in the same manner as he does for an unwitting transgression. From where do we derive this halakha?
messages.quote: the oath of testimony

messages.text: With regard to all those who are liable to bring a sliding-scale offering, it is stated: “And it be hid from him” (see Leviticus 5:2–4). But here, with regard to the oath of testimony (Leviticus 5:1), it is not stated: And it be hid from him. This omission serves to render him liable for an unwitting transgression in the same manner as an intentional transgression.
messages.lead: It is as the Sages taught in a baraita:

notes.he: בכל המביאין עולה ויורד שבאותה פרשה כגון מטמא מקדש ושבועת בטוי דכתיבי בהו שבועת העדות:
notes.en: In all of them: in all who bring a sliding-scale offering in that passage, such as one who renders the Temple impure and the oath of utterance, which are written together with the oath of testimony.

messages.text: The mishna teaches that one who falsely takes the oath on a deposit brings an offering for an intentional transgression as he does for an unwitting transgression. From where do we derive this halakha?
messages.quote: the oath on a deposit

messages.text: The tanna derives it from a verbal analogy between the term “shall sin,” stated with regard to an oath on a deposit (Leviticus 5:21), and the term “shall sin,” stated with regard to the oath of testimony (Leviticus 5:1). It is derived from this verbal analogy that just as in the case of the oath of testimony one is liable for committing an intentional transgression in the same manner as an unwitting transgression, the same applies to the oath on a deposit.

§ The mishna teaches: There are five individuals who bring one offering for several transgressions, i.e., for violating the same transgression several times. Among them, the tanna teaches: One who engages in several acts of intercourse with an espoused maidservant. From where do we derive this halakha?
messages.quote: one who engages in several acts of intercourse with an espoused maidservant

messages.text: The verse states: “And the priest shall make atonement for him with the ram of the guilt offering before the Lord for his sin that he has sinned” (Leviticus 19:22). The superfluous phrase “that he has sinned” teaches that he brings one offering for several transgressions.
messages.lead: It is as the Sages taught in a baraita:

verse.he: וְכִפֶּר עָלָיו הַכֹּהֵן בְּאֵיל הָאָשָׁם לִפְנֵי יְהֹוָה עַל־חַטָּאתוֹ אֲשֶׁר חָטָא וְנִסְלַח לוֹ מֵחַטָּאתוֹ אֲשֶׁר חָטָא׃ {פ}
verse.en: With the ram of reparation offering the priest shall make expiation for him before GOD for the sin that he committed; and the sin that he committed will be forgiven him.

messages.text: Furthermore, the verse concludes: “With the ram of the guilt offering before the Lord for his sin that he has sinned; and he shall be forgiven for his sin that he has sinned.” The second instance of the phrase “that he has sinned” serves to render the halakha with regard to an intentional transgression the same as it is with regard to an unwitting transgression, that one brings a guilt offering in either case.

But when this verse is written, it is written with regard to an intentional transgression, as the verse states: “There shall be an inspection” (Leviticus 19:20), which indicates a punishment of lashes, and lashes are given only for an intentional transgression.
messages.quote: to render the halakha with regard to an intentional transgression the same as it is with regard to an unwitting transgression

verse.he: וְאִישׁ כִּי־יִשְׁכַּב אֶת־אִשָּׁה שִׁכְבַת־זֶרַע וְהִוא שִׁפְחָה נֶחֱרֶפֶת לְאִישׁ וְהׇפְדֵּה לֹא נִפְדָּתָה אוֹ חֻפְשָׁהֿ לֹא נִתַּן־לָהּ בִּקֹּרֶת תִּהְיֶה לֹא יוּמְתוּ כִּי־לֹא חֻפָּשָׁה׃
verse.en: If a man has carnal relations with a woman who is a slave and has been designated for another man, but has not been redeemed or given her freedom, there shall be an indemnity; they shall not, however, be put to death, since she has not been freed.

notes.dh: לעשות מזיד כשוגג והא עיקר קרא במזיד כתיב
notes.he: דכתיב (ויקרא י״ט:כ׳) בקורת תהיה והיינו מלקות ואין מלקות אלא במזיד ועליה קאמר והביא את אשמו ותו למה לי ונסלח לו מחטאתו לרבות מזיד:
notes.en: To make intentional like unwitting; but the verse itself is written about intentional sin: for it is written: “There shall be an inspection [bikoret]” (Leviticus 19:20), which is lashes, and there are lashes only for intentional sin; and about that it says: “And he shall bring his guilt offering.” Why, then, do I need “and he shall be forgiven for his sin” to include intentional sin?

notes.he: דמביאין קרבן עולה ויורד כתיב בהו ונעלם וכאן לא כתיב. והא קרא כי כתיב ואיש כי ישכב את אשה שכבת זרע והיא שפחה במזיד כתי'. מדכתיב בקורת תהיה דהיינו מלקות אלמא דמזיד הוא וכתיב וכפר עליו הכהן לעשות מזיד לקרבן שוגג איבעי ליה למימר:
notes.en: In all of them: those who bring a sliding-scale offering, “and it be hid” is written about them, and here it is not written. But when the verse is written, “And a man who lies carnally with a woman, and she is a maidservant,” it is written about intentional sin, since it is written “there shall be an inspection,” which is lashes; evidently it is intentional. And it is written: “And the priest shall make atonement for him”; so instead of “to make intentional [like unwitting]” for an offering, he should have said unwitting [like intentional].

messages.text: Rather, say that the language of the baraita should be reversed, as follows: The phrase “that he has sinned” renders the halakha with regard to an unwitting transgression to be the same as it is with regard to an intentional transgression.

notes.he: דמהו דתימא דוקא אמזיד מביא ולא אשוגג קא משמע לן ונסלח לו מחטאתו אשר חטא דלהכי כתיב חטא ארבע זימני תרי למילף קרבן אחד על עבירות הרבה ותרי לעשות שוגג כמזיד:
notes.en: Rather, say: to make unwitting like intentional: for you might have said that he brings [an offering] only for intentional sin and not for unwitting sin. It teaches us: “And he shall be forgiven for his sin that he has sinned.” That is why “sin” is written four times: two to derive one offering for many transgressions, and two to make unwitting like intentional.

messages.text: If one engages in intercourse with five espoused maidservants [shefaḥot ḥarufot] in one lapse of awareness, meaning that he was not informed of the prohibition in between his unwitting transgressions, what is the halakha? Is he liable to bring an offering for each and every one, or is he liable to bring only one offering?
messages.lead: Rabbi Ḥanina of Tirna’a raised a dilemma before Rabbi Yoḥanan:

notes.he: כלומר קודם שילקה ויביא קרבן על זו חזר ובעל זו:
notes.en: In one lapse of awareness: that is, before he was flogged and brought an offering for this one, he went back and had relations with that one.

notes.he: ששגג שלא ידע שהתורה אסרן:
notes.en: In one lapse of awareness: that he erred, not knowing that the Torah forbade them.

messages.text: He is liable to bring an offering for each and every one.
messages.quote: for each and every one, or is he liable to bring only one offering

messages.text: What is different about this instance compared to the case of five lapses of awareness with regard to one espoused maidservant, when he brings only one offering, as stated in the mishna?

notes.he: ומאי שנא מחמש העלמות בשפחה אחת דאינו מביא אלא קרבן אחד כדתנן והבא על השפחה ביאות הרבה:
notes.en: And what is different from five lapses of awareness with one maidservant, where he brings only one offering, as we learned [in the mishna]: “And one who engages in several acts of intercourse with a maidservant”?

messages.text: In a case of multiple transgressions with one espoused maidservant, there are not separate bodies, as he committed multiple transgressions with the same individual. By contrast, in a case of separate transgressions with five espoused maidservants, there are five separate bodies, and therefore each one requires a separate offering.
And from where do we derive that there is halakhic significance to the separate bodies in the case of an espoused maidservant?
messages.lead: Rabbi Ḥanina further asked Rabbi Yoḥanan:

messages.text: Did you not state with regard to those with whom relations are forbidden that when the verse states: “And you shall not approach unto a woman to uncover her nakedness, as long as she is impure by her uncleanness” (Leviticus 18:19), this serves to require separate offerings for each and every woman with whom one committed unwitting transgressions?

verse.he: וְאֶל־אִשָּׁה בְּנִדַּת טֻמְאָתָהּ לֹא תִקְרַב לְגַלּוֹת עֶרְוָתָהּ׃
verse.en: Do not come near a woman during her menstrual period of impurity to uncover her nakedness.

notes.he: בפ"ק (לעיל כריתות ב:) ואל אשה לחלק על כל אשה ואשה כו':
notes.en: Did you not say about forbidden relations: in the first chapter (above, 2b): “And unto a woman,” to divide for each and every woman, and so on.

messages.text: With regard to an espoused maidservant it is also similarly written: “And if a man lies carnally with a woman,

notes.he: הכא נמי האי שפחה דכתב לחלק כתיב דהא מצי למיכתב ואיש אשר ישכב את אשה שכבת זרע:
notes.en: “And unto a woman,” to divide: here too, this “maidservant” is written to divide, for it could have written: “And a man who lies carnally with a woman.”

messages.text: 9b
and she is a maidservant designated to a man” (Leviticus 19:20). This verse likewise serves to require separate offerings for each and every espoused maidservant.

verse.he: וְאִישׁ כִּי־יִשְׁכַּב אֶת־אִשָּׁה שִׁכְבַת־זֶרַע וְהִוא שִׁפְחָה נֶחֱרֶפֶת לְאִישׁ וְהׇפְדֵּה לֹא נִפְדָּתָה אוֹ חֻפְשָׁהֿ לֹא נִתַּן־לָהּ בִּקֹּרֶת תִּהְיֶה לֹא יוּמְתוּ כִּי־לֹא חֻפָּשָׁה׃
verse.en: If a man has carnal relations with a woman who is a slave and has been designated for another man, but has not been redeemed or given her freedom, there shall be an indemnity; they shall not, however, be put to death, since she has not been freed.

notes.dh: והיא שפחה לחלק על כל שפחה ושפחה
notes.he: תימה דהכא בעינא לחלק אע"ג דגופין מוחלקין והתם פרק אותו ואת בנו (חולין פב:) לא תשחטו ביום אחד משמע דפשיטא דחייב גבי שחטה ואח"כ שחט בניה משום דגופין מוחלקין אע"ג דליכא קרא וכן לקמן בפרק אמרו לו (כריתות דף יז.) דאמרי שבתות כי גופין דמיין:
notes.en: “And she is a maidservant,” to divide for each and every maidservant: this is puzzling: here we need [a verse] to divide even though the bodies are separate, whereas there, in the chapter Oto VeEt Beno (Ḥullin 82b), [on] “you shall not slaughter on one day,” it implies that it is obvious he is liable [twice] where he slaughtered it and then slaughtered its offspring, because the bodies are separate, even though there is no verse; and likewise below, in the chapter Amru Lo (Keritot 17a), where they say that Shabbatot are like separate bodies.

messages.text: § The mishna teaches: A nazirite who became ritually impure with several instances of contact with ritual impurity brings one offering for several transgressions. Who is the tanna that taught this?
messages.quote: a nazirite who became ritually impure due to several instances of contact with ritual impurity

notes.he: מאן תנא ר' יוסי בר' יהודה היא כולה הא שמעתא דנזיר פרשינן בריש פירקין קמא:
notes.en: (Up to here belongs to 9a.) And a nazirite who became impure several times: who is the tanna? It is Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Yehuda. This entire discussion of the nazirite we explained at the beginning of our first chapter.

messages.text: It is the opinion of Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Yehuda, who says: A new naziriteship of purity, which is required of a nazirite who became ritually impure, takes effect from the seventh day of the nazirite’s purification.
messages.quote: Who is the tanna that taught this?

notes.he: הלכך כי נטמא תרי זימני בשביעי הוו להו טומאות הרבה דהא אתחלא נזירות דטהרה ולענין קרבן לא מחייב אלא אחד דלא יצא אדם זה לשעה ראויה לקרבן:
notes.en: The naziriteship of purity takes effect from the seventh: therefore, when he became impure twice on the seventh, these are many impurities, since the naziriteship of purity had begun; and with regard to an offering he is liable only once, since this man had not emerged into a time fit for an offering.

messages.text: And therefore, you find that the nazirite brings one offering for several transgressions in a case where he became impure on the seventh day of his purification, was pure for seven days, and again became impure on the seventh day of his purification. And since for each case where he became impure the appropriate time to sacrifice an offering, i.e., the eighth day of his purification, had not yet emerged, he is liable to bring only one offering.

The mishna must be in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Yehuda, as if it follows the opinion of Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi, then it is not possible for a nazirite to bring one offering for several transgressions, since Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi says: A new naziriteship of purity does not take effect until a nazirite’s eighth day of purification.

If there was a case where a nazirite became impure on the seventh day of his purification, was pure for seven days, and then became impure again on the seventh day of his purification, according to Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi, that is all one long period of impurity, as the new term of naziriteship has not yet begun, and therefore the nazirite brings one offering for the entire period.

And if there was a case where a nazirite became impure on the eighth day of his purification, was pure for seven days, and then again became impure on the eighth day of his purification, then since the appropriate time to sacrifice an offering had emerged, he is obligated to bring an offering for each and every time he became impure.
Rather, conclude from it that the mishna is in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Yehuda.
And what is the statement of Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Yehuda? As it is taught in a baraita:

The verse states with regard to a nazirite who begins a new naziriteship of purity after having become impure: “And on the eighth day he shall bring two doves or two pigeons…And the priest shall prepare one for a sin offering and the other for a burnt offering, and make atonement for him, for that he sinned by reason of the dead; and he shall sanctify his head on that day” (Numbers 6:10–11). This teaches that the new term of naziriteship begins on the day of the bringing of his offerings, which is the eighth day of his purification. This is the statement of Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi.

verse.he: וּבַיּוֹם הַשְּׁמִינִי יָבִא שְׁתֵּי תֹרִים אוֹ שְׁנֵי בְּנֵי יוֹנָה אֶל־הַכֹּהֵן אֶל־פֶּתַח אֹהֶל מוֹעֵד׃ וְעָשָׂה הַכֹּהֵן אֶחָד לְחַטָּאת וְאֶחָד לְעֹלָה וְכִפֶּר עָלָיו מֵאֲשֶׁר חָטָא עַל־הַנָּפֶשׁ וְקִדַּשׁ אֶת־רֹאשׁוֹ בַּיּוֹם הַהוּא׃
verse.en: On the eighth day they shall bring two turtledoves or two pigeons to the priest, at the entrance of the Tent of Meeting. The priest shall offer one as a purgation offering and the other as a burnt offering, and make expiation on [the nazirite’s] behalf for the guilt incurred through the corpse. That same day their head shall be reconsecrated;

notes.he: שנזירות טהרה חלה עליו. יום תגלחתו כו':
notes.en: “And he shall sanctify his head”: that the naziriteship of purity takes effect on him. On the day of his shaving, and so on.

messages.text: The verse means that the new term of naziriteship begins on the day of his shaving, i.e., the seventh day of his purification.

messages.caption: The same dispute, drawn for Keritot 2b: does the new naziriteship of purity begin on the seventh day or the eighth?

messages.text: Mishna

Third, one who issues a warning to his wife declaring himself jealous with regard to several different men with whom he suspects her of committing adultery, and forbidding her to be alone with them. If the wife was then found separately in seclusion with each of the men, he brings her to the Temple with one single meal offering of jealousy.
messages.lead: The mishna continues to list the five situations in which one offering is brought to atone for several transgressions:

notes.he: מביא מנחת שעורים אחת על כולן כשהוא משקה:
notes.en: Mishna. One who warns his wife, etc.: he brings one barley meal offering for all of them when he has her drink.

messages.text: And fourth, a leper who was afflicted with several instances of leprosy, meaning that he was purified from his leprosy, and before he brought his offerings, he suffered a relapse of the leprosy. When he is finally purified, he brings only one set of offerings.

notes.he: כגון שספר שבעה ולא הספיק להביא קרבנותיו עד שנתנגע וכן שניה וכן שלישית:
notes.en: Who was afflicted with many afflictions: for example, he counted seven [days] and did not manage to bring his offerings before he was afflicted [again], and likewise a second time, and likewise a third.

messages.text: If a leper brought the two requisite birds on the first day of his purification (see Leviticus 14:4–7), and prior to bringing his offerings on the eighth day of his purification he was afflicted with a relapse of leprosy, those birds do not satisfy his obligation until he brings his sin offering.

notes.he: אותן שתי צפרין חיות אחת לשחיטה ואחת לשילוח ולאו קרבן נינהו:
notes.en: He brought birds: those two live birds, one for slaughter and one for sending away; and they are not an offering.

notes.he: קס"ד דהאי לא עלו לו משמע שצריך לחזור ולהביא לבסוף שתי צפרין לכל נגע ונגע עד שיביא חטאת אבל הביא צפרין וחטאתו ונתנגע אין צריך להביא לכשיטהר על נגע ראשון:
notes.en: They do not count for him: it now enters our mind that this “they do not count for him” means that at the end he must again bring two birds for each and every affliction, until he brings a sin offering; but if he brought birds and his sin offering and was then afflicted, he need not bring [birds] for the first affliction when he becomes pure.

notes.he: כשנרפא מצרעתו ולא הספיק להביא חטאתו עד שחזר ונתנגע וחזר ונרפא והביא ציפרין ונתנגע קודם שהביא חטאתו ואשמו כשחזר ונתרפא צריך להביא ציפרין אחרים וחטאת על כל נגע שלא עלו לו הראשונות עד שיביא חטאתו עמהן:
notes.en: He brought birds: when he was healed from his leprosy and did not manage to bring his sin offering before he was afflicted again, and he was healed again and brought birds, and was afflicted before he brought his sin offering and his guilt offering. When he is healed again he must bring other birds, and a sin offering for each affliction, for the first ones do not count for him until he brings his sin offering with them.

messages.text: Until he brings his guilt offering.

notes.dh: ר' יהודה אומר עד שיביא אשמו
notes.he: עמהן:
notes.en: Rabbi Yehuda says: until he brings his guilt offering: with them.

messages.text: Gemara

The mishna teaches that if a man issues a warning to his wife with regard to several different men, and the wife violates the warning and is secluded with each of them, he brings one meal offering of jealousy. From where do we derive this halakha?
messages.quote: one who issues a warning to his wife declaring himself jealous with regard to several different men

messages.text: It is as it is written: “This is the law of jealousies, when a wife, being under her husband, goes aside, and is defiled” (Numbers 5:29). The plural form of the word “jealousies,” teaches that one law, meaning one sacrificial offering, can suffice for several jealousies, i.e., different warnings.

verse.he: זֹאת תּוֹרַת הַקְּנָאֹת אֲשֶׁר תִּשְׂטֶה אִשָּׁה תַּחַת אִישָׁהּ וְנִטְמָאָה׃
verse.en: This is the ritual in cases of jealousy, when a woman goes astray while in her husband’s household and defiles herself,

notes.he: תימה דבסוטה אמרינן לרבנן אין אשה שותה ושונה ולר' יהודה באיש אחד ושני בועלים אינה שונה וכיון דאינה שונה למאי איצטריך דלא מייתי אלא קרבן אחד:
notes.en: One law for many jealousies: this is puzzling: for in Sota we say that according to the Rabbis a woman does not drink [the water] a second time, and according to Rabbi Yehuda, with one husband and two adulterers she does not drink a second time. And since she does not drink a second time, why is it necessary [to teach] that he brings only one offering?

messages.text: The mishna teaches that a leper who was afflicted with several instances of leprosy brings one single offering. From where do we derive this halakha?
messages.quote: a leper who was afflicted with several instances of leprosy

messages.text: It is as it is written: “This shall be the law of the leper in the day of his purification” (Leviticus 14:2). The term “the law” teaches that one law, meaning one sacrificial offering, can suffice for several lepers, i.e., for several instances of leprosy in the same individual.

verse.he: זֹאת תִּהְיֶה תּוֹרַת הַמְּצֹרָע בְּיוֹם טׇהֳרָתוֹ וְהוּבָא אֶל־הַכֹּהֵן׃
verse.en:
This shall be the ritual for a leper, a person afflicted with ṣaraʻath; see note at 13.3. at the time of being purified.
When it has been reported to the priest,

notes.he: ובתורת כהנים מפיק ליה מדכתיב וכבשה אחת מלמד שמביא אחת על נגעים הרבה ומוזאת תהיה תורת דריש תורה אחת לכל מצורעין לפי שמצינו שחלק הכתוב בטומאותיהם ובשבועותיהם:
notes.en: One law for many lepers: and in Torat Kohanim it derives this from what is written: “And one ewe lamb” (Leviticus 14:10), which teaches that he brings one for many afflictions; and it expounds “This shall be the law” as one law for all lepers, because we found that the verse distinguished among them in their impurities and in their weeks [of quarantine].

messages.text: § The mishna teaches: If a leper brought the two birds on the first day of his purification, and prior to bringing his offerings on the eighth day of his purification he was afflicted with a relapse of leprosy, those birds do not satisfy his obligation until he brings his sin offering. Rabbi Yehuda says: Until he brings his guilt offering. This apparently means that when he is healed from the relapse of his leprosy, he must bring additional birds to fulfill the obligation generated by the first instance of leprosy.
messages.quote: those birds do not satisfy his obligation until he brings his sin offering

messages.text: But didn’t you say in the mishna that he brings only one set of offerings for several instances of leprosy?
messages.quote: he brings only one set of offerings

notes.dh: גמ' והאמרת אינו מביא אלא קרבן אחד
notes.he: על נגעים הרבה אלמא חד צרעת אריכתא היא ואמאי מחייבת ליה לאתויי צפרים אכל נגע:
notes.en: Gemara. But didn’t you say that he brings only one offering: for many afflictions? Evidently it is one long leprosy. Why, then, do you obligate him to bring birds for each affliction?

notes.dh: והא אמרת אינו מביא אלא קרבן אחד
notes.he: על נגעים הרבה:
notes.en: But didn’t you say that he brings only one offering: for many afflictions?

messages.text: The text of the mishna is incomplete, and this is what it is teaching: In the case of a leper who was afflicted with several instances of leprosy and was subsequently purified from his leprosy, if he brought the two birds, and was then afflicted with a relapse of leprosy, he brings only one set of offerings.

notes.dh: חסורי מחסרא והכי קתני הביא ציפרין כו' אין מביא אלא קרבן אחד
notes.he: והאי דקאמר לא עלו עד הכי קאמר ולאקבועי בעניות ובעשירות לא מיקבע עד שיבא חטאת כלומר אם היה עני והביא חטאתו בעניות אע"ג דקודם שהביא אשמו וציפרין נתעשר הכל הולך אחר חטאת ויביא הכל בעניות:
notes.en: It is incomplete, and this is what it teaches: he brought birds, and so on; he brings only one offering. And what it says, “they do not count until,” this is what it means: and with regard to establishing [his status] in poverty or wealth, it is not established until he brings the sin offering. That is, if he was poor and brought his sin offering in poverty, then even though he became wealthy before he brought his guilt offering and birds, everything follows the sin offering, and he brings everything in poverty.

messages.text: But with regard to establishing whether a leper has a status of poverty or of affluence in order to determine whether he brings a poor man’s offering or a rich man’s offering (see Leviticus, chapter 14), that is not established until he brings his sin offering.

notes.he: וה"ק ולא עלו הצפרין ליקבע בעניות ובעשירות דאם היה עני בשעת הבאת צפרין והעשיר צריך להביא קרבן עשיר ואם היה עשיר והעני מביא עני בדלות עד שיביא חטאתו דבתר חטאת אזלינן בין בעניות בין בעשירות:
notes.en: And to establish [his status] in poverty, etc.: and this is what it says: the birds do not count to establish [his status] in poverty or in wealth. For if he was poor at the time he brought the birds and then became wealthy, he must bring a wealthy man’s offering; and if he was wealthy and became poor, he brings a poor man’s [offering] in his poverty; [this is so] until he brings his sin offering, for we follow the sin offering, whether in poverty or in wealth.

notes.he: או אם היה עשיר והפריש חטאת בהמה והעני ימתין עד שיעשיר ויביא הכל בעשירות:
notes.en: Or if he was wealthy and set aside an animal sin offering and became poor, he should wait until he becomes wealthy and bring everything in wealth.

messages.text: The leper’s status of poverty or affluence is not established until he brings his guilt offering.

notes.he: ר' יהודה אומר עד שיביא אשמו דסבר הכל הולך אחר אשם:
notes.en: Rabbi Yehuda says: until he brings his guilt offering: for he holds that everything follows the guilt offering.

messages.text: We learned in a mishna there (Nega’im 14:11):
messages.lead: The Gemara cites a dispute that supports this interpretation:

messages.text: In a case of a leper who was poor when he brought his guilt offering and then became wealthy before bringing the other offerings, all differences in offerings between a leper with the status of a rich man or a poor man follow his status at the time he brought his sin offering; this is the statement of Rabbi Shimon.
It all follows his status at the time he brought his guilt offering.
It all follows his status at the time he brought the two birds.
messages.lead: The Gemara cites an additional opinion: It is taught in a baraita:

messages.text: All three of them interpreted the same verse to arrive at their respective opinions: “This is the law of he who has the mark of leprosy, whose means do not suffice for that which pertains to his purification” (Leviticus 14:32).

verse.he: זֹאת תּוֹרַת אֲשֶׁר־בּוֹ נֶגַע צָרָעַת אֲשֶׁר לֹא־תַשִּׂיג יָדוֹ בְּטׇהֳרָתוֹ׃ {פ}
verse.en: Such is the ritual for one who has a scaly affection and whose means for purification are limited.

notes.he: בשעת טהרתו יביא בעניות אע"פ שהעשיר:
notes.en: “Whose means do not suffice”: at the time of his purification he brings [the offering] in poverty, even though he later became wealthy.

messages.text: Rabbi Shimon holds that the term “his purification” is referring to the matter that atones for his sin, i.e., the sin offering.

notes.he: האי טהרתו היינו דבר המכפר חטאו דעל ז' דברים נגעים באין במסכת ערכין (דף טז.):
notes.en: Rabbi Shimon holds: this “his purification” is the thing that atones for his sin, for afflictions come on account of seven things, in tractate Arakhin (16a).

notes.he: היינו חטאת:
notes.en: Atones for him: this is the sin offering.

messages.text: Rabbi Yehuda holds that it is referring to the matter that renders him fit to consume sacrificial meat, which is the guilt offering.

notes.he: אשם שמדמו נותנין על בהונותיו מכשירו בקדשים:
notes.en: The thing that renders him fit: the guilt offering, from whose blood they place on his thumbs; it renders him fit for sacrificial food.

notes.he: היינו אשם:
notes.en: Renders him fit for sacrificial food: this is the guilt offering.

messages.text: And Rabbi Eliezer ben Ya’akov says that it is referring to the matter that causes him to return to a state of purity. And what are these? The birds.

notes.he: גורמין לו תחלת טהרתו שמדם הצפור מזין עליו:
notes.en: Birds: they cause him the beginning of his purification, for they sprinkle on him from the blood of the bird.

notes.he: ציפרין כדכתיב ולקח למטהר שתי צפרים חיות טהורות:
notes.en: Causes him purity: the birds, as it is written: “Then the priest shall command to take for him that is to be cleansed two living, pure birds” (Leviticus 14:4).

messages.caption: Which of the leper’s offerings fixes whether he brings a poor man’s or a rich man’s offering, and how each Tanna reads “his purification.”

messages.text: Mishna

A woman who gave birth to several offspring. This is a case where a woman gave birth to a daughter, after which she is ritually impure for fourteen days and then enters a period of sixty-six days of ritual purity, even if she experiences uterine bleeding. Nevertheless, during this interim period, she is still somewhat impure, and it is therefore prohibited for her to enter the Temple or to partake of consecrated food, and at the end of the period she must bring an offering.
messages.lead: The mishna continues with the last of the five situations in which one offering is brought to atone for several transgressions:

notes.he: וקא מפרש כיצד כגון שהפילה לתוך פ' של נקבה וכו' כגון שטבלה לאחר שבועיים דטומאה ושמשה ונתעברה והפילה נקבה לאחר מ' של יצירת הולד דהיינו נ"ד ללידה ראשונה וחזרה והפילה לסוף נ"ד של זו. ולהכי נקט נקבה דבזכרים ליכא למימר הכי דאי הפילה בתוך מ' דזכר מיא בעלמא הוא האי שני דאין הולד נוצר עד יום מ':
notes.en: Mishna. A woman who gave birth to several offspring: and it explains how: for example, she miscarried within the eighty [days] of a female, and so on. For example, she immersed after the two weeks of impurity, had relations, conceived, and miscarried a female after the forty days of the formation of the fetus, which is fifty-four [days] after the first birth; and she again miscarried at the end of fifty-four days after this one. And that is why it speaks of a female, for with males one cannot say so: if she miscarried within the forty [days] of a male, this second one is mere water, for the fetus is not formed until the fortieth day.

messages.text: And during those days of ritual purity, she became pregnant again and then miscarried a female fetus within the eighty days, and then became pregnant again and miscarried another female fetus within eighty days of the first miscarriage. In this situation, when she ultimately completes her process of purification, she brings one single offering for all the births and miscarriages.

notes.he: האשה שהפילה ולדות הרבה בתוך מלאות וכדפירש במתניתין הפילה בתוך שמונים כו' מביאה קרבן אחד על כולן:
notes.en: The woman who miscarried many offspring within the completion [periods], as explained in the mishna: she miscarried within eighty, and so on; she brings one offering for all of them.

messages.text: And a similar halakha applies to a woman who miscarries multiple fetuses from a single pregnancy at different points in time, miscarrying each fetus before completing the purification period of forty days for a male or eighty days for a female for the previous fetus. When she finally completes her process of purification, she brings one single offering for all of the miscarriages.

notes.he: אפילו זכרים כגון שנתעברה ג' והפילה אחד לאחר מ' והשני נשתהה ויצא בתוך ימי טוהר הראשון ושלישי בתוך ימי טוהר דשני מביאה קרבן אחד על האחרון ופטורה:
notes.en: And one who miscarries twins: even males. For example, she conceived three, and miscarried one after forty [days], and the second was delayed and came out within the days of purity of the first, and the third within the days of purity of the second: she brings one offering, for the last, and is exempt [for the others].

messages.text: In these cases, a single offering does not suffice for all the births or miscarriages. Rather, she brings an offering for the first birth or miscarriage and does not bring an offering for the second miscarriage, as it took place before the completion of the purification period for the first. She then brings an offering for the third miscarriage and does not bring an offering for the fourth fetus, as it was miscarried before the completion of the purification period for the third fetus.

notes.he: פליג בין אולדות בין אתאומין ואמר מביאה קרבן אחד על הראשון על הולד הראשון ולא על השני מפני שנולד בתוך מלאת של ראשון ומביאה על השלישי משום דהוא לא נולד תוך מלאת דלא חשבינן מלאת לשני דכמאן דליתיה דמי הואיל ונולד תוך מלאת של ראשון ושלישי הוי תחילת לידה ואינה מביאה קרבן על הרביעי הואיל ונולד תוך (מ') מלאת של שלישי אבל שלישי לא נולד תוך מלאת דראשון דהא עברו ימי טומאה דראשון (ויצירת שני וטומאתו ויצירת שלישי) דהוי טפי מפ' לראשון וגבי תאומים נמי דקפליג ר' יהודה כגון שנולד שלישי לאחר מלאת דראשון ועל מלאת דשני לא איכפת לו דכמאן דליתיה דמי:
notes.en: Rabbi Yehuda disagrees both about [separate] offspring and about twins, and says: she brings one offering for the first, for the first offspring, and not for the second, because it was born within the completion [of the purification days] of the first. And she brings [one] for the third, because it was not born within a completion, for we do not count a completion for the second, which is as though it does not exist, since it was born within the completion of the first; and the third is the beginning of a [new] birth. And she does not bring an offering for the fourth, since it was born within the completion of the third. But the third was not born within the completion of the first, for there have passed the days of impurity of the first (and the formation of the second and its impurity, and the formation of the third), which is more than eighty from the first. And with twins as well, where Rabbi Yehuda disagrees: for example, where the third was born after the completion of the first; and he is not concerned with the completion of the second, which is as though it does not exist.

messages.text: Gemara

The mishna teaches that a woman who gave birth to several offspring brings a single offering. From where do we derive this halakha? As the tanna taught a baraita before Rav Sheshet with regard to the verse:
messages.quote: A woman who gave birth to several offspring

messages.text: “This is the law for the woman who bears a child, whether a male or a female” (Leviticus 12:7). This teaches that she brings one offering for several offspring.

verse.he: וְהִקְרִיבוֹ לִפְנֵי יְהֹוָה וְכִפֶּר עָלֶיהָ וְטָהֲרָהֿ מִמְּקֹר דָּמֶיהָ זֹאת תּוֹרַת הַיֹּלֶדֶת לַזָּכָר אוֹ לַנְּקֵבָה׃
verse.en: He shall offer it before GOD and make expiation on her behalf; she shall then be pure from her flow of blood. Such are the rituals concerning a woman who bears a child, male or female.

notes.he: כל היכא דכתיב תורת משמע רבים:
notes.en: Gemara: wherever “the law of” [torat] is written, it implies many.

messages.text: One might have thought that she brings one single offering even in a case where she becomes purified simultaneously both for a birth and for an irregular discharge of blood from the uterus [ziva]. Therefore, the verse states: “This,” to exclude such a case.

notes.he: קרבן אחד כגון שראתה ג' ימים בימי זיבה והפסיקה רביעי וילדה בחמישי הרי זו יולדת בזוב כדאמרי' בנדה (דף לו:) דבעי שתפסוק מן הזוב סמוך ללידה ואם לא פסקה ודאי דם מחמת הולד ואינה יולדת בזוב:
notes.en: One might have thought: for the birth and for the ziva [one offering]: for example, she saw [blood] for three days during the days of ziva, stopped on the fourth, and gave birth on the fifth. This is one who gives birth in zov, as we say in Nidda (36b) that she must stop from the discharge close to the birth; and if she did not stop, it is certainly blood caused by the fetus, and she is not one who gives birth in zov.

notes.he: שאם ילדה בזוב וכדתנן במס' נדה המקשה הרי זו נדה קישתה ג' ימים בתוך י"א שבין נדה לנדה ושפת מעת לעת שלא ראת דם הרי זו זבה ואח"כ ילדה הרי זו יולדת בזוב ומביאה ב' קרבנות אחד על הלידה ואחד על הזיבה נפטרת נמי בקרבן אחד:
notes.en: One might have thought: even for the birth and for the ziva: that if she gave birth in zov, as we learned in tractate Nidda (36b): “A woman who has difficulty in labor is a nidda; if she had difficulty for three days within the eleven days between one menstrual period and the next, and had a full day’s respite in which she did not see blood, she is a zava,” and afterward she gave birth, this is one who gives birth in zov, and she brings two offerings, one for the birth and one for the ziva. [One might have thought that] she is also exempted with one offering.

messages.text: The tanna teaches: One might have thought that even in a case where she completes her purification at the same time for a birth and for ziva, she should bring only one offering. If that is so, then in a case where she consumed blood unintentionally, and is therefore liable to bring a sin offering, and she also gave birth, might one also have thought that she should bring only one offering?
messages.quote: both for a birth and for an irregular discharge

notes.he: מהיכא תיסק דעתיה דעל הלידה ועל הזיבה קרבן אחד דאיצטריך קרא למעוטי הא ודאי אכלה חלב וילדה מי סלקא אדעתין דמביאה קרבן אחד על הלידה ועל החלב וגבי זיבה נמי מה ענינה אצל לידה:
notes.en: If that is so: from where would it enter his mind that for the birth and the ziva there is one offering, so that a verse was needed to exclude it? Certainly, if she ate forbidden fat and gave birth, would it enter our minds that she brings one offering for the birth and for the fat? And with ziva too, what does it have to do with birth? [Rashi reads “ate forbidden fat”; the daf reads “consumed blood.”]

messages.text: That is illogical, as these offerings are two completely different obligations. So too, the offerings after childbirth and ziva are two separate obligations.

notes.he: כלומר דעל הוולדות מביא קרבן אחד אבל לא על הלידה ועל הזיבה [אלא מעתה] אכלה חלב וילדה אכלה דם וילדה הכי נמי דאין מביאה אלא קרבן אחד אלא כשם שמביאה ב' קרבנות על חלב ועל לידה כך מביאה ב' קרבנות על לידה ועל זיבה:
notes.en: The verse states “this”: that is, for the offspring she brings one offering, but not for the birth and for the ziva. [If that is so,] if she ate forbidden fat and gave birth, or ate blood and gave birth, so too would she bring only one offering?
